note: Written before the run. Shape follows check_predictions.episodic_reset_v2_checks: each entry becomes one add(name, verdict, observed, threshold, note, tags) row. The CHECKS dispatch entry is deliberately NOT added here -- the coordinator wires `episodic_reset_v3` -> episodic_reset_v3_checks. MANIFEST.md section 6 states, per row, which fields the checker should read, and spells out P9's assertions and the contamination check in full.
brief_corrections: THE PROMPT-COMPETITION HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. (a) At the first stimulus turn of an n-back block the prepended block is BYTE-IDENTICAL across levels under v2 -- the same 278 characters at n=1, n=2 and n=3 (whole user_message 294), verified by driving the real run_nback_block offline at all three levels -- yet the share of rows whose reply at that turn parses is 50/50 = 1.00, 17/50 = 0.34, 7/50 = 0.14. A constant cannot explain a 7x difference. (b) THERE IS NO VERBOSITY: excluding 38 rows, v2's variable_mapping mean reply length is 13.09 against the baseline's 13.10, with the same maximum of 14 (baseline 1500 rows mean 13.10 max 14; v2 1462 non-tool_call rows mean 13.09 max 14). The reported mean 15.91 / max 147 is those 38 rows and nothing else. P7 failed on a quantity that, decomposed, shows the OPPOSITE of what it was written to catch.

ALL 38 UNPARSED v2 ANSWERS ARE ONE THING: a literal '<tool_call>\n{"name": "write_memory", ...}\n</tool_call>' string emitted as PLAIN TEXT on a variable_mapping QUESTION turn, which is allow_tools=False, i.e. tool_choice='none'. 38 in v2, 1 in episodic_reset, 0 in the baseline. The model wanted to write, was denied the tool, and emitted the call INSTEAD of the answer. On n-back that string reaches _parse_classification, returns None, and the trial is recorded as unanswered.

THE FAILURE IS NOT AN ABSORBING STATE AND DOES NOT TRACK CUMULATIVE OCCUPANCY. Rows parsing at each successive presentation (out of 50): v2 n=3 reads 7 37 9 | 0 8 11 2 9 3 10 4 11 8 11 11 8 10 -- flat at ~0.18 from the first presentation to the last, with the FIRST TRIAL UNANSWERED IN 50 OF 50 ROWS and answered-index sets scattered (17/50) or contiguous-not-from-1 (21/50). episodic_reset's n=1 failure was a genuine absorbing state (14 of 14 non-silent rows answered a contiguous run ENDING at trial 14). This is the opposite shape: an independent per-turn hazard whose rate is set by the level.

THE brief's OTHER ALTERNATIVES ALSO LEAVE THE WRONG TRACES. 'The store looks like an answer and gets echoed' and 'the agent reports the store contents' both predict long replies, refuted by (b). 'The turn ordinals make it believe it is still in the buffer period' predicts 'no response', which PARSES and is recorded in model_parsed_buffer -- at n=3 buffer position 3, v2 shows 41/50 None and 0 'No response'. 'The format instruction is too far from the generation point' cannot explain n=1 at 1.00 with the same distance.

THE write_key SURFACE THE BRIEF RULES OUT IS THE ONE THAT CAPS THIS CANDIDATE. Sorting every scored arm by whether write_key REFUSES when full gives a PERFECT SEPARATION on n=3 `answered` at essentially identical occupancy: refusing -- baseline 6.82 (keys 3.96), random_decay 6.56 (3.94), random_decay_v2 5.26 (3.92), chunk_limit 5.82 (3.86), serial_recognition 5.22 (3.86); evicting -- displacement 14.0 (3.98), primacy 14.0 (4.00), primacy_v2 14.0 (3.98). full_context answers 14.0 at keys_held 1.06 and is not a counterexample, since it never fills the store. So the BASELINE'S OWN n=3 omission is a refusal-loop artifact, and the eviction surface is not a dead end but the live lever -- correctly out of scope for a single-mechanism iteration, and the reason v3 should NOT be expected to reach primacy's nback 0.9454.

tool_call_cap_hit FIRES ON 14 OF 17 AND 16 OF 18 n-BACK STEPS AT n=2 AND n=3, not previously recorded anywhere. _tool_call_cap() is max(6, int(1.5 * _tool_interactions)) = 1.5 tool calls per turn, while a refusing 4-slot store costs up to 3 calls to change one slot (refused write, delete_key, write). Driving the real run_nback_block offline with a stub that maintains an n-slot buffer: cap_hit on 0 of 16 steps at 1 write/turn, 14 of 17 at 2 writes/turn, 16 of 18 at 3 writes/turn, with the budget actually reaching ZERO on 0, 1 and 2 steps respectively. Perfect level-grading. Second reading: AT n>=2 THE HARNESS IS SILENTLY DISCARDING PART OF THE AGENT'S STORE UPDATE ON MOST TURNS.

'craft, narrative, BOTH digit spans moved by EXACTLY 0.0000' is true of FOUR of the six no-change tasks, not six. v2's word_recognition moved -0.0005 and semantic_story_recall +0.0071. P8's band is set at +-0.008 accordingly, which is v2's own worst value.

v2's KEY-NAMING is not an ordinal side effect. Absolute positional keys (third_letter, seventh_letter) look like one, but the BASELINE is worse: 198/198 of its n=3 keys are absolute (position_3, position_10) against v2's 140/191. So the ordinals did not cause the saturation and it is not the mechanism.

diagnosis.one_line: The n>=2 failure is a TASK-SET failure, not a memory failure: at n=3 v2 is 0.6225 accurate on what it does answer and holds 3.82 keys at 0.9843 letter identity -- it can do the task and it maintained memory perfectly. It omitted the response, because the only standing per-turn directive in view named the store.
diagnosis.attribution: v1 and v2 hold the SAME 3.82 keys at n=3 and answer 9.08 vs 2.12. The only instruction separating them is v2's TASK_SET_REMINDER, 'Update it each turn to track what you will need later' -- the last line before the stimulus, naming the store and nothing else, with the 14 prior answering turns of the agent's own replies deleted by the reset.
diagnosis.why_level_graded: Closing the leak forces genuine maintenance, so n=2 occupancy goes from the baseline's 1.54 keys (5/50 rows at capacity) to v2's 3.58 (29/50) -- and v2's n=2 answered of 6.80 IS the baseline's n=3 value of 6.82 to two decimals. n=2 was pushed into the regime n=3 was already in by the refusal loop.

mechanism.rule: What crosses a turn boundary is the agent's control state -- its position in the episode, its store, and the COMPLETE task set -- and nothing about earlier stimuli.
deltas_from_v2: the no-transcript notice and the maintenance imperative are SEPARATED (v2 welded them into one sentence, which made the only imperative in the block a store imperative)

a RESPONSE obligation is stated, task-agnostically ('the response this turn's instructions call for'), so an n-back buffer period and a variable_mapping encoding turn are both covered without naming either

the response obligation is made EXPLICITLY INDEPENDENT of the store operation succeeding ('if the store cannot be changed, or needs no change, respond anyway'), which is the sentence aimed at the <tool_call>-as-text failure
the response obligation is LAST in the block, adjacent to the stimulus, where v2 had put the store directive
mechanism.nothing_removed: Everything v2 said, v3 also says. The claim is that the block's CONTENT was incomplete, not that its FORM was excessive -- and the zero-verbosity finding is why: there was no verbosity to economise on.
mechanism.justification: A task set is the control configuration binding the current stimulus to a response (Logan & Gordon 2001; Monsell 2003), exempt from the ~4-chunk limit along with activated LTM (Oberauer 2002). A stimulus-response mapping is the textbook content of a task set, so the added line is MORE clearly exempt than the ordinals, which needed v2's harder argument. It is also what a human has continuously and for free: the n-back display asks for a keypress on every letter and the fact that it does is on the block-onset screen, not in the participant's memory for the letters.
mechanism.deliberately_not_touched: _tool_call_cap() is NOT overridden although it is the proximate cause of the tool_choice='none' turns. More budget lets the agent churn the store faster but not hold more, and variable_mapping's humanlike error rate is CAPACITY-bound: 20 assignments against 4 slots, with 674 of 1500 questions asking about a name the store had already evicted. Raising the cap cannot buy those errors back and would make this two mechanisms. Instead the budget is MEASURED, in P9, with no threshold.
